ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a galvanic cell apparatus. In the left half-cell there is a Cu electrode, and the solution is labeled CuNO3; in the right half-cell there is a Zn electrode, and the solution is labeled Zn(NO3)2; the two sides are connected by the upper wire and the salt bridge in the middle labeled NaBr. The overall reaction given below the image is: 2Cu+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Cu(s) + Zn2+(aq), E° = +1.28 V. Reasoning: The question asks how many moles of electrons need to be transferred to produce 127 g of copper. According to the method draft, using the molar mass of copper as 63.5 g/mol, 127 g Cu ÷ 63.5 g/mol = 2.00 mol Cu. From the reaction in the figure, 2Cu+ is reduced to form 2Cu(s); each Cu+ gains 1 electron, so producing 1 mol Cu requires 1 mol electrons. Producing 2.00 mol Cu therefore requires 2.00 mol electrons.

Half-Cell A: Strip of Cu(s) in $CuNO_3(aq)$
Half-Cell B: Strip of Zn(s) in $Zn(NO_3)_2(aq)$
When the cells are connected according to the following diagram, the following reaction occurs. How many moles of electrons must be transferred to create 127g of copper?

method.method_draft: First describe the image setup and read the balanced reaction shown under the galvanic cell. Convert 127 g Cu to moles using 63.5 g/mol, giving about 2.00 mol Cu. From the displayed reaction, 2Cu+ are reduced to 2Cu(s), requiring 2 electrons total, so the electron-to-copper ratio is 1 mol e− per 1 mol Cu. Therefore 2.00 mol Cu requires 2.00 mol electrons.

method.method_draft: First describe the cell image, noting the Cu/CuNO3 half-cell and that the problem asks about forming solid copper. Determine the oxidation state of copper in CuNO3 as +1 because nitrate is −1. Write the copper reduction half-reaction Cu+ + e− -> Cu(s). Convert 127 g Cu to moles: 127/63.5 ≈ 2 mol Cu. Since each mole of Cu(s) formed consumes one mole of electrons, 2 mol Cu requires 2 mol electrons.
